title: IEA Oil Market Report (September 2026)
source: EST: investing.com's IEA Monthly Oil Market Report calendar page lists the next release as "Sep 11, 2026 09:00", against a printed history of Aug 12, Jul 10, Jun 17, May 13, Apr 14, Mar 12, Feb 12 2026 and Dec 11 2025 that matches the IEA's own monthly cadence; a second independent search read returned the same 11/09/2026 date and the IEA's standing 10:00 Paris release time. AGGREGATOR-SOURCED AND LABELLED AS SUCH — iea.org returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl on 2026-09-06, so the primary schedule page could not be read this session and this date has not been checked against it. STAYS ESTIMATE, but the table it comes from earned a reliability check during the 2026-09-06 initial research: IEA's own asset host iea.blob.core.windows.net does serve (HTTP 200), and its OMR PDF filenames encode release dates, so four of the same aggregator table's back-history rows were compared against IEA primaries and matched 4/4 exactly — -11DEC2025_OilMarketReport.pdf, -21JAN2026_OilMarketReport.pdf, -14APR2026_OilMarketReport_Free_version1.pdf, -13MAY2026__OilMarketReport_publicversion.pdf. That is a check on the table, not on the Sep-11 row, which remains unread at source; the status stays estimate on three counts that are not date doubt — the primary schedule page 403s, this file's source-prefix taxonomy defines no IEA: confirmed prefix, and the event-research lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Release time independently corroborated at 10:00 Paris = 04:00 ET. Re-checked 2026-09-06
notes: The missing IEA-side checkpoint in the Hormuz supply story. opec-plus-meeting-2026-09-06 has leaned on an IEA figure it could never verify at source — its D-4 row quotes the IEA at ~10 mb/d of Gulf shutdowns from an Argus headline whose body did not fetch — while the only dated energy-supply publication this calendar tracks is the US-side eia-steo-2026-09-09. This is the other agency's number, on a date, so the ~2x published spread on Hormuz flow (4.9 mb/d AIS-derived vs 8-10 mb/d US-government/Goldman) gets a third independent read instead of staying a two-source disagreement. Filed low on the same reasoning as eia-steo-2026-09-09 and opec-jmmc-68th-2026-10-04: a forecast publication sets no policy and moves no equity tape. It also lands on the most crowded macro day of the month - August CPI (cpi-2026-09-11), mts-august-2026-09-11, umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-09-11 and sp-rebalance-proforma-capped-2026-09-11 all print the same session - so treat it as a data source to read after the fact, never as a scheduled catalyst. Discovered during the opec-plus-meeting-2026-09-06 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-06).
